Setzer's signature amp for decades — his 2023 Premier Guitar Rig Rundown confirms he still tours with a pair of early-'60s Fender Bassman 6G6-B heads, preferring them for their solid-state rectifier and tight bass response.
Guitar World notes Setzer's main rig since 1981 has consistently been a 1963 Fender Bassman head with matching 2x12 cabinet, pushed to the edge of clean headroom for his rockabilly tone.
The broader Bassman 'tweed' family is closely associated with Setzer's sound; earlier tweed-era circuit variants appear in his collection alongside the 6G6-B brownface units.
The Ramones' standard live rig featured Marshall heads running multiple 4x12 cabinets, defining the raw, stripped-down street/punk guitar sound from the mid-70s onward.
Cock Sparrer's quintessential street punk tone is widely associated with a Marshall JCM800 — the go-to amp recreated by fans covering their songs, prized for its biting, overdriven character.
Steve Jones' ferocious Sex Pistols rhythm tone — a foundational influence for all street punk — was built around cranked Marshall JMP heads, inspiring countless punk players after him.
Ginn famously produced his brutal, raw hardcore/street punk sound using a solid-state Randall amp pushed extremely loud, a tone that influenced the harder side of the street punk genre.
Bavarian indie-rock bands of their era commonly relied on Marshall JCM 800s for their punchy, mid-forward crunch tone, consistent with Sportfreunde Stiller's live guitar sound.
The AC30 is a staple of European indie-rock guitarists seeking chimey cleans and natural breakup, fitting the jangly, melodic guitar tones heard on albums like 'You Have to Win Zweikampf'.
The Fender Blues Deluxe's warm, clean headroom suits the melodic, mid-tempo indie rock of Sportfreunde Stiller and is a common choice for German indie guitarists of the 2000s.
The Ampeg SVT is a standard choice for bass players in rock trios needing a full, punchy low end to anchor a guitar-drums-bass format like Sportfreunde Stiller's.
